The usual mistake is to believe in Democracy as the best thing.

Think of Condorcet's paradox: By trying to make all parts equally happy, Democracy makes every choice a shift toward the most mediocre solution because your voice counts the same as an idiot's.

What do we really want? We want the dedicated/capable people to take the best decisions in our interest. Maybe by weighting each elector's voice according to his knowledge of what's being decided... Or maybe by having specialists performing the votes.

So, either we take the ability to vote properly into account, or we choose an aristocratic way of functioning (from the Greek: "power to the most brilliant")... or we also shift this step and elect a benevolent dictator, like both China and UK did: Xi or the (aging) Queen.

I personally go with a third solution: limiting each country to a max of 8'000'000 inhabitants to avoid huge mass-manipulation effect. I like the Swiss model because it's fair and it works.
